abilities.description: Choreographs crowds and sightlines so attention lands exactly where she wants it.
abilities.name: Grand Misdirection

abilities.description: Palms and swaps small objects under close observation.
abilities.name: Sleight of Hand

abilities.description: Plans multi-stage operations with cues, backups and escape routes.
abilities.name: Heist Staging

characters.arc: Starts as a flamboyant leader who treats every job as applause. At the Aerie, the Silent Overture's sabotage plunges the lights into chaos, and she must abandon her elaborate finale and carry out a plain, silent retrieval in the dark, trusting Pell's improvisation over her script. She ends as a leader who values the crew's safety above spectacle, and she takes a quiet bow instead of a grand one.
characters.description: Ringmaster and lead illusionist of the Curtain Call Company, a lean woman in her forties with silver-streaked auburn hair, ink-stained gloves and a coat lined with trick pockets. Raised in the wings of the Gilded Lantern Theatre, she inherited the troupe after its previous director lost his shadow to a cursed mask and faded from memory. She plans every heist like a stage show, with cues, reversals and a final bow.
characters.external_conflict: The Lanternwrights' Guild hunts her crew while the Silent Overture works to sabotage the heist at the Aerie.
characters.flaw: Compulsive showmanship: she cannot resist adding a flourish to a plan, even when simplicity would be safer.
characters.goal: Steal the Obsidian Earring from the duchess's reliquary and return it to felt-lined darkness before it awakens.
characters.internal_conflict: She fears she is repeating her mentor's fatal pride, yet only theatrical daring has ever made her feel worthy of leading.
characters.motivation: To keep the memory of her faded mentor alive by proving the troupe's thefts protect Velmire rather than plunder it.
characters.name: Marisol Vane

abilities.description: Shapes and stretches his own shadow to shield or mask others.
abilities.name: Shadow Weaving

abilities.description: Climbs rigging and mooring lines with ease.
abilities.name: Rooftop Agility

characters.arc: Begins as an eager apprentice who takes risks to prove himself. When the Aerie's chandeliers blaze and the earring begins to stir, he lets his own shadow be stretched across the guests to hold the relic dormant, nearly losing it. He ends as a measured performer who accepts that belonging does not depend on being irreplaceable.
characters.description: A wiry young shadow-weaver and the Company's newest member, with soot-dark eyes and a patched velvet waistcoat. Orphaned when the fog took his family's lamp shop, he learned to coax his own shadow into small tricks on the Gilded Lantern Theatre's stage, where the lights cast the sharpest shadows in the city.
characters.external_conflict: The earring's awakening threatens to devour his shadow first, since he is the one who works most closely with shadows.
characters.flaw: Reckless overconfidence in his own untested talent.
characters.goal: Use his shadow craft to shield the crew's shadows from the earring during the heist.
characters.internal_conflict: He wants to be indispensable but dreads that his shadow tricks are what make him valuable rather than himself.
characters.motivation: To earn a permanent place in a family that chooses him, after losing his own.
characters.name: Pell Ashgrove

abilities.description: Builds intricate mechanical props and gadgets from scrap.
abilities.name: Clockwork Artifice

abilities.description: Modifies lamp output to dim, flicker or fail on cue.
abilities.name: Aether Lamp Tuning

characters.arc: Starts as a bitter exile who builds alone. During the Aerie job, her dampener fails under the awakening relic's interference, and she accepts Tobias Wren's guidance on Guild vault techniques that she had always rejected. She ends reconciled with her craft and no longer needing the Guild's blessing.
characters.description: The Company's mechanician, a broad-shouldered woman in her fifties with brass-rimmed goggles and burn-scarred hands. A former Lanternwrights' apprentice, she left the Guild after it refused to repair the Velvet Vault's failing seals, and she now builds the troupe's clockwork props and aether-lamp dampeners.
characters.external_conflict: Her former Guild colleagues treat her as a traitor and hunt the crew she now serves.
characters.flaw: Stubborn pride that makes her refuse help and ignore warnings about her designs.
characters.goal: Build a clockwork device that suppresses aether lamps near the reliquary so the crowd never triggers the earring.
characters.internal_conflict: She still craves the Guild's approval while resenting it for abandoning the vault.
characters.motivation: To prove her old Guild wrong by mending the failures it ignored.
characters.name: Orsolya Thistlewick

abilities.description: Understands the behaviors and triggers of cursed antiquities.
abilities.name: Relic Lore

abilities.description: Steers nobles and servants through flattery and veiled threats.
abilities.name: Courtly Manipulation

characters.arc: Begins as a serene orchestrator who sees victims as notes in a score. When the Aerie's lights flicker out and his own shadow begins to fade at the relic's touch, he faces the unmaking he praised. He ends desperate and frightened, trying to halt the awakening he engineered.
characters.description: Archivist-prelate of the Order of the Silent Overture, a gaunt man with pale lashes and gloves of grey silk, who moves through society as an elegant collector. He was once a Guild scholar who witnessed a theatre troupe lose its shadows and concluded that such unmaking was a form of transcendence.
characters.external_conflict: The Curtain Call Company's heist threatens to put the earring back to sleep before it awakens.
characters.flaw: Cold detachment that blinds him to the human cost of his plans.
characters.goal: Ensure the earring is exposed to the full ballroom under bright light, and block the Company's attempt to remove it.
characters.internal_conflict: He has begun to fear that his own shadow is already thinning from years among cursed relics.
characters.motivation: To witness the earring's awakening as proof that shadow-devouring is a sublime release rather than a tragedy.
characters.name: Lysander Mourne

abilities.description: Commands deference and obedience from nobles and servants.
abilities.name: Court Authority

abilities.description: Hides fear and intent behind perfect poise.
abilities.name: Masked Composure

characters.arc: Begins as a confident hostess who laughs off danger. When the chandeliers blaze and guests start turning pale, she must choose between her pride and her guests, and she orders the ballroom darkened and the reliquary opened to Marisol. She ends humbled but respected for putting her guests ahead of her trophy.
characters.description: Mistress of the Aerie and head of the Court of Gilded Masks, a statuesque woman in her sixties with a silver half-mask and a voice like polished glass. Her house raised the floating ballroom and bought the Obsidian Earring at auction to display as a status trophy.
characters.external_conflict: Thieves and the Silent Overture both target her prized possession during her ball.
characters.flaw: Vanity that makes her dismiss any warning that might spoil her entertainment.
characters.goal: Host a flawless ball that dazzles the court and keeps the earring safely on show.
characters.internal_conflict: She privately fears the relic and her own fading status, but cannot admit weakness before the court.
characters.motivation: To secure her house's rank by owning and displaying the most dangerous relic in Velmire.
characters.name: Duchess Ilvane Corvaine

abilities.description: Knows felt-lining and silence techniques that quiet cursed relics.
abilities.name: Vault Wardcraft

abilities.description: Wields a clockwork aether staff to light, bind and repel.
abilities.name: Lantern Staff

characters.arc: Starts as an unbending pursuer of thieves. After finding the Velvet Vault's seals cracking and the Company's plan the only practical way to put the earring back to sleep, he chooses to share Guild vault knowledge with Orsolya rather than arrest her. He ends as an ally who bends procedure to protect the city.
characters.description: A senior warden of the Lanternwrights' Guild, a stooped man in his sixties with a brass lantern staff and a patient manner. He has guarded the Velvet Vault for decades and watched its seals weaken, though he will not say so aloud.
characters.external_conflict: The Company's meddling and the Silent Overture's schemes undermine his control over the relics.
characters.flaw: Rigid adherence to oath and procedure, even when it fails.
characters.goal: Capture the Curtain Call Company and secure the Obsidian Earring in the Velvet Vault.
characters.internal_conflict: He knows the vault is failing, yet admitting it would betray the Guild he has served all his life.
characters.motivation: To keep the Guild's ancient oath to protect the city from its most dangerous relics.
characters.name: Tobias Wren

relationships.description: Marisol Vane trains Pell Ashgrove as her protege, but her showy plans push him to take risks with his shadow craft that she cannot control.
Pell Ashgrove idolizes Marisol Vane and bends his plans to win her approval, which amplifies his recklessness.
Marisol Vane relies on Orsolya Thistlewick's devices, but her flourishes strain Orsolya's practical designs and stubborn pride.
Lysander Mourne schemes to sabotage Marisol Vane's heist at the Aerie so the earring awakens, directly opposing her goal of returning it to sleep.
Marisol Vane sees Lysander Mourne as the embodiment of the cold fascination that destroyed her mentor, and she is determined to outmaneuver him.
Tobias Wren hunts Marisol Vane for meddling with relics under Guild oath, even as the failing vault shows he may need her.
Orsolya Thistlewick resents Tobias Wren for the Guild's refusal to mend the vault seals, while he regards her as a traitor to the oath they once shared.
Duchess Ilvane Corvaine welcomes Lysander Mourne as a respected collector at her ball, unaware he plans to use her guests to awaken the earring.
Duchess Ilvane Corvaine guards her earring against thieves like Marisol Vane, whose heist threatens her status before the court.
